skills.name: Trade blocs: forms and distinguishing features

note.text: A trade bloc is an arrangement between economies to organise aspects of exchange. In a simplified comparison, a free-trade area removes agreed internal trade barriers while members retain their own external tariffs. A customs union adds a common external tariff. A common market adds freer factor movement. A monetary union shares monetary arrangements. Actual agreements vary and implementation can differ from stated aims.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to classify an invented arrangement from its stated integration features. Builds on: trade measures and cross-border connections. Leads to: regional opportunities and limitations.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: Invented Region K removes agreed internal tariffs but keeps separate external tariffs: it fits our free-trade-area model. Region L also adopts a common external tariff: it fits the customs-union model. Neither description proves all border checks disappear or that every person has unrestricted movement. These are feature cards, not current rules for travellers or traders.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Underline the distinguishing feature. Separate internal trade from treatment of non-members, and goods movement from labour or capital movement. Use the stated model rather than assuming every bloc follows an identical compulsory sequence.
